content.text: [{"sha":"2feed0ce9363debe4df6b0d0829639bd5f383299","html_url":"https://github.com/archestra-ai/archestra/commit/2feed0ce9363debe4df6b0d0829639bd5f383299","commit":{"message":"fix(apps): bound app tool calls at the LLM ceiling and cancel abandoned calls (#6963) ## Summary An app's `archestra.llm.complete()` rejected with `MCP error -32001: Request timed out` whenever the attached model needed more than 60 seconds — which reasoning models routinely do, since the app path is the platform's only non-streaming LLM call and all thinking time accumulates into the single response (T-981). The timer was the MCP SDK's default request timeout in the app iframe's guest client: the SDK passed no request options to `callServerTool`, and nothing downstream was stricter, so the guest always lost the race while the backend kept generating (and the proxy kept billing) a result nobody would receive. Live measurement on a dev stack: the app showed the error at exactly 60s while the same completion returned HTTP 200 at 100s and was recorded in LLM logs ~40s after the app had already failed. The guest now bounds host tool calls at 10 minutes, matching the platform's own upstream LLM client ceiling (`ANTHROPIC_CLIENT_TIMEOUT_MS`) rather than gating stricter than it. Cancellation travels the whole chain: the guest's timeout or teardown aborts the host bridge's fetch via the `oncalltool` handler's `extra.signal`; the app proxy route closes the per-request transport when the client disconnects, which makes the protocol abort the in-flight handler's signal; that signal reaches `executeArchestraTool` (as the existing `context.abortSignal`) and `executeToolCallForOwner` (its existing `abortSignal` option); and an aborted LLM completion stops quietly instead of logging an error and claiming `llm_unavailable`. Two route-level details deserve reviewer attention. In JSON-response mode an aborted handler never produces a response, so `transport.handleRequest` never settles — the route races it against the client-disconnect path instead of awaiting it bare. And an aborted request leaves its transport closed mid-flight, so the per-(app,user) cached server is evicted rather than released for reuse; the cache's exclusive `acquire` guarantees the closed transport can only ever belong to the aborted request. ## Validation - `app-sdk-runtime.test.ts`: the guest-module stub now honors the MCP SDK's request-options timeout contract; new tests pin that a 3-minute completion resolves (red before this fix, failing with the exact reported error) and that a completion beyond the 10-minute ceiling still times out. - `app-llm.test.ts`: an aborted call cancels the model call and reports cancellation, not a provider failure. - Live on a dev stack with a reasoning model (glm-5.1): a 188-second completion resolves in the real iframe chain where it previously died at 60s; killing the viewer 25 seconds into a call produced the cancelled tool-call record within ~1 second. ## Follow-up The LLM proxy's non-streaming handlers do not tie their own upstream request to their client's disconnect, so a cancelled completion can still run to completion inside the proxy and record the interaction (observed landing two minutes after the abort). That gap predates this change, spans every provider adapter, and equally affects non-streamed chat cancellation — left for its own change. No docs change: the apps page never promised a timeout, and the fix restores its documented behavior (`llm.complete` resolves to the model's text). --- ","author":{"name":"Mark Novikov","email":"piercypixel@gmail.com","date":"2026-07-29T16:51:18Z"},"committer":{"name":"GitHub","email":"noreply@github.com","date":"2026-07-29T16:51:18Z"}},"author":{"login":"piercypixel","id":13911621,"profile_url":"https://github.com/piercypixel","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/13911621?v=4"},"committer":{"login":"web-flow","id":19864447,"profile_url":"https://github.com/web-flow","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/19864447?v=4"}},{"sha":"1dd549c91308beee38066bbc75e1baaf7af97ebc","html_url":"https://github.com/archestra-ai/archestra/commit/1dd549c91308beee38066bbc75e1baaf7af97ebc","commit":{"message":"fix(github-copilot): verify model invocability at sync, surface an actionable model-not-supported error (#6964) Fixes T-959: chat on the GitHub Copilot provider could fail with `400 {"message": "The requested model is not supported.", "type": "api_validation_error"}` for models Archestra itself offered in the model picker. ## Root cause Copilot's `/models` is not an invocability catalog. Verified against a live subscription: 13 of the 24 entries our static filter kept were rejected outright by `/chat/completions` with `model_not_supported` — retired aliases listed next to their still-working snapshots (`gpt-4` vs `gpt-4o`, `gpt-3.5-turbo` vs `gpt-3.5-turbo-0613`), client-internal agent models (`copilot-search-*`, `exec-agent-*`), and per-plan-unavailable models that still declare `"/chat/completions"` in `supported_endpoints`. No catalog field discriminates dead from alive entries (a dead alias can be field-identical to a working model, down to `version`), and on the verified plan every entry is `model_picker_enabled: false`, so no static filter can compute the usable set. GitHub's own clients avoid the problem only because their picker never exposes these entries. ## Fix **Verify invocability during model sync.** CAPI validates the model before the payload, so a deliberately invalid `{"model": …, "messages": []}` request is a zero-inference oracle: a dead model answers `model_not_supported`, a live one answers "messages must be non-empty". Nothing is generated and no model is ever invoked, so the probe cannot consume premium requests. The fetcher now probes every statically-kept candidate (8 concurrent) and drops only definite `model_not_supported` answers — 429/5xx/network failures keep the model, so an upstream outage degrades to the previous unverified catalog rather than an empty one. Runs everywhere the fetcher is used: connect-time key validation, lazy re-sync, explicit sync, and the proxy `/models` listing. **Actionable error for the residual window.** A conversation can stay pinned to a model that has since died (the proxy's error wrapping keeps `message`/`type` but drops the upstream `code`). The chat error mapper now classifies Copilot's model-not-supported 400 as `NotFound` — "The selected model is not available. Please choose a different model." — instead of the retry-suggesting invalid-request copy, which misleads on a deterministic rejection. ## Testing - New proxy route tests drive the real adapter and Copilot fetch wrapper (token exchange + editor-identity headers) against a faked wire, pinning that the catalogued model name goes upstream and the upstream 400 surfaces for both streaming and non-streaming. - New chat stream test pins that a github-copilot conversation's model FK is dereferenced to the provider model name before dispatch. - Fetcher tests cover the verification: a listed-but-rejected model is dropped, probes only target statically-kept candidates, inconclusive probes (429/network) keep the model. - Error-mapper tests cover the NotFound classification and that other Copilot 400s keep the generic invalid-request code. - Live validation on a dev stack with a real subscription: synced catalog went from 24 models (13 dead) to the invocable set; picking any listed model chats successfully; a conversation pinned to a dead model shows the actionable copy. --- ","author":{"name":"Mark Novikov","email":"piercypixel@gmail.com","date":"2026-07-29T16:45:51Z"},"committer":{"name":"GitHub","email":"noreply@github.com","date":"2026-07-29T16:45:51Z"}},"author":{"login":"piercypixel","id":13911621,"profile_url":"https://github.com/piercypixel","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/13911621?v=4"},"committer":{"login":"web-flow","id":19864447,"profile_url":"https://github.com/web-flow","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/19864447?v=4"}},{"sha":"1a1fd231e171822cd869f84c7e3346b59e76fbfb","html_url":"https://github.com/archestra-ai/archestra/commit/1a1fd231e171822cd869f84c7e3346b59e76fbfb","commit":{"message":"ci: revert run heavy test suites only in the merge queue (#6615) (#6801) Restores the heavy test suites (backend unit test shards + gate, frontend integration tests, and both Rust checks) to run on pull_request pushes again, reverting PR #6615 which had moved them to merge-queue-only behind a run-unit-tests label. This regressed dev experience: contributors could no longer confirm their tests passed on their own branch and instead had to iterate through the merge queue, where "new tests showing up" is unexpected. The original author-based bot-pr-guard is restored on each suite (bot PRs still skip), the `labeled` trigger and run-unit-tests escape hatch are removed, and later mac-mini runner routing plus the mac-mini-watchdog job are preserved untouched. Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Mc1gaHM4iHWsFeBYK7M9sg --- Co-authored-by: Claude Co-authored-by: Joey Orlando ","author":{"name":"Ildar Iskhakov","email":"ildar6v@gmail.com","date":"2026-07-29T15:22:41Z"},"committer":{"name":"GitHub","email":"noreply@github.com","date":"2026-07-29T15:22:41Z"}},"author":{"login":"iskhakov","id":2262529,"profile_url":"https://github.com/iskhakov","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/2262529?v=4"},"committer":{"login":"web-flow","id":19864447,"profile_url":"https://github.com/web-flow","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/19864447?v=4"}},{"sha":"2cb4a589217f3511054924e1e5e8e5de7b290b72","html_url":"https://github.com/archestra-ai/archestra/commit/2cb4a589217f3511054924e1e5e8e5de7b290b72","commit":{"message":"chore(mcp): stop declaring the roots capability no client implements (#6960) Follow-up nit from the #6953 chat-client review. All three MCP client constructions (chat loopback client, both upstream client paths in `mcp-client.ts`) declared `roots: { listChanged: true }` — but no `roots/list` handler exists anywhere in this codebase, so a server acting on the declaration always got method-not-found. Roots is also deprecated in 2026-07-28. Removing a client capability only reduces what servers attempt; nothing that worked can break. Verified: `tsc`, `biome ci`, `knip` clean; 157 tests across `mcp-client` and the chat-client suites pass. --- ","author":{"name":"Joey Orlando","email":"joey@archestra.ai","date":"2026-07-29T14:51:50Z"},"committer":{"name":"GitHub","email":"noreply@github.com","date":"2026-07-29T14:51:50Z"}},"author":{"login":"joeyorlando","id":9406895,"profile_url":"https://github.com/joeyorlando","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/9406895?v=4"},"committer":{"login":"web-flow","id":19864447,"profile_url":"https://github.com/web-flow","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/19864447?v=4"}},{"sha":"18695c1387be23097b27b6fbe5034ba3a2aa67cd","html_url":"https://github.com/archestra-ai/archestra/commit/18695c1387be23097b27b6fbe5034ba3a2aa67cd","commit":{"message":"feat(mcp-gateway): subscriptions/listen and x-mcp-header support (#6953) Continues the 2026-07-28 work after #6952. Now carries both remaining protocol features (#6954 was merged into this branch); Tasks stays separate (#6956). ## subscriptions/listen (SEP-2575) - New `routes/mcp-gateway/subscriptions.ts`: long-lived SSE stream handled at the route (the SDK transport only does single JSON responses). - Honors `toolsListChanged` only — tool lists are local DB, detected by fingerprint polling (20s); prompt/resource lists are upstream-aggregated, so those types are omitted from the ack per spec. - Ack-first ordering, subscription id (= listen request id) on every notification, graceful-close response, SSE keep-alives. - `tools.listChanged` now advertised `true` for 2026-07-28 clients (backed by the stream); legacy stays `false`. - Legacy clients calling the method get `-32601`; a listen without an id is rejected. ## x-mcp-header (SEP-2243) - New `clients/mcp-param-headers.ts`: annotation validation (token syntax, uniqueness, primitive types, static reachability) and value encoding (decimal ints, lowercase booleans, `=?base64?...?=` wrapper for unsafe values). - Invalid tool definitions are excluded from `tools/list` with a warning; valid annotations mirror argument values into `Mcp-Param-{name}` headers on upstream calls. - Per-call headers ride the passthrough-header pipeline; the existing credential-fingerprint check rebuilds pooled connections when the header set changes, so values can't leak across calls. - Assignment queries now project the tool input schema so the call path reads annotations without an extra lookup. ## Tests / checks - 9 unit + 4 real-socket route tests for subscriptions; 29 unit + 2 transport-level integration + 1 route test for x-mcp-header. - 396 pass across the gateway/client suites; `biome ci`, `tsc`, `knip`, docs link check clean. - Fixes the biome `noControlCharactersInRegex` error that failed #6954's CI (house ignore pattern on the RFC 9110 byte-range regex). ## Docs Gateway page: feature-table rows for change notifications and `x-mcp-header`, plus a client note for subscriptions.","author":{"name":"Joey Orlando","email":"joey@archestra.ai","date":"2026-07-29T14:51:31Z"},"committer":{"name":"GitHub","email":"noreply@github.com","date":"2026-07-29T14:51:31Z"}},"author":{"login":"joeyorlando","id":9406895,"profile_url":"https://github.com/joeyorlando","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/9406895?v=4"},"committer":{"login":"web-flow","id":19864447,"profile_url":"https://github.com/web-flow","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/19864447?v=4"}},{"sha":"40fe0314f3c722cb6358c48cd4dbecd3484cc798","html_url":"https://github.com/archestra-ai/archestra/commit/40fe0314f3c722cb6358c48cd4dbecd3484cc798","commit":{"message":"fix(llm-cost): price the OpenAI Codex models the registry omits (#6957) ## Summary models.dev carries the `gpt-5.3` generation onward but never backfilled the Codex and `chat-latest` models before it. Nothing resolves them, so each one reaches the fabricated default estimate: `gpt-5.1-codex` recorded at $50/M against a published $1.25/M, `gpt-5.1-codex-mini` at $30/M against $0.25/M — a 120× overstatement on a model people run all day. That estimate is not cosmetic. It flows into `interactions.cost`, the cost statistics, optimization-rule savings and token-cost limits. Prices for the eight affected ids are transcribed from OpenAI's own price list and placed at the bottom of the ladder, below the registry. The map can only fill what models.dev omits and cannot override an entry it already carries, so the 62 OpenAI rows the registry prices today cannot move. When the registry catches up the map stops being consulted and can be deleted; a PR adding these models upstream is the follow-up. Every id is stated outright rather than derived by stripping `-codex` to reach a base model. The suffix predicts the price for `gpt-5.1-codex`, which bills exactly what `gpt-5.1` does, and then breaks immediately on `gpt-5.1-codex-mini` at a fifth of it. Inferring a price from a name that resembles a sibling's is the failure this repo already removed once, for the family-matched AWS entries. The proxy's discovery path needed the same fill. It falls back to a first-party registry entry, which finds nothing for these models, so a discovered row kept the estimate for its whole life. That lookup ignores the provider the row was written under: the proxy records a discovered model against the *endpoint's* provider, so naming a Codex model on a Bedrock endpoint produces a `bedrock` row, and a reseller publishing no rate of its own has nothing better to offer than the model's own price. It also covers a second shape. models.dev publishes entries whose `cost` is an empty object, meaning the vendor sets no per-token rate — that entry resolves, so the row was previously enriched with its context and limits while the price alone fell through to the estimate. ## Verification Against the running app, a sync moves exactly the eight rows and nothing else — no row added, none removed, no other provider's price changed: ``` chat-latest 50.00/50.00 -> 5.00/30.00 gpt-5-chat-latest 50.00/50.00 -> 1.25/10.00 gpt-5-codex 50.00/50.00 -> 1.25/10.00 gpt-5.1-chat-latest 50.00/50.00 -> 1.25/10.00 gpt-5.1-codex 50.00/50.00 -> 1.25/10.00 gpt-5.1-codex-max 50.00/50.00 -> 1.25/10.00 gpt-5.1-codex-mini 30.00/30.00 -> 0.25/2.00 gpt-5.2-codex 50.00/50.00 -> 1.75/14.00 ``` The capability matrix carries the three new resolution paths. Its unpriced ratchet consults the published map, so a priced discovery row is not miscounted as falling through — the guard would otherwise quietly lose its meaning. ## Known gap These rows report `priceSource: "models_dev"`, which is wrong; the price came from OpenAI's list. Provenance is re-derived at read time by comparing the stored value against the AWS map rather than recorded when the price is written, so it cannot name a tier it does not know about. That predates this change — it already mislabels 48 Bedrock rows — and fixing it properly means recording the winning tier at write time. Left for that work rather than bolting a half-right label on here. --- ","author":{"name":"Alexander Balashov","email":"22360+divineforest@users.noreply.github.com","date":"2026-07-29T14:42:47Z"},"committer":{"name":"GitHub","email":"noreply@github.com","date":"2026-07-29T14:42:47Z"}},"author":{"login":"divineforest","id":22360,"profile_url":"https://github.com/divineforest","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/22360?v=4"},"committer":{"login":"web-flow","id":19864447,"profile_url":"https://github.com/web-flow","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/19864447?v=4"}},{"sha":"7bc0ff3262d277b328cd4d87370cc13193df6b8f","html_url":"https://github.com/archestra-ai/archestra/commit/7bc0ff3262d277b328cd4d87370cc13193df6b8f","commit":{"message":"fix(a2a): reject contentless message turns instead of sending them to the provider (#6959) ## Summary An A2A `SendMessage` whose only text part is empty or whitespace passed the execute gate but produced no current user turn, so the agent re-sent the conversation's prior context verbatim. Prior context always ends with the agent's last reply, so the request reached the provider terminating on an assistant message. Recent Claude models no longer support assistant prefill and reject such a request with a 400, which surfaced to users as the generic "There was an issue with your request. Please try again." The gate and the executor disagreed on what counts as content: `needToExecute` asks whether any part exists, while the executor builds a current user turn only from text that survives `trim()`. A blank text part satisfies the first and not the second. Blank text parts are now dropped when assembling `messageParts`, so both conditions read the same input. A contentless turn returns the existing `Nothing to execute` error (`-32602`), never reaches the provider, and no longer persists an empty user message into context history. A blank part mixed with real text also stops contributing a stray separator to the joined turn the model receives. Blank text falls through to the file branch rather than returning early, so a part carrying both blank text and a file keeps its payload — otherwise an attachment-only turn would be rejected, since `needToExecute` is evaluated before attachments are collected. Task resumption via `taskOps` is unaffected: it executes through `taskWasSwitchedToWorkingState`, independent of message parts. Known behavior change worth a reviewer's attention: a blank-text turn carrying an ephemeral execution prefix — chatops server-side sessions, where a 1:1 message has no text, no delivered attachment, and no skipped-attachment note — previously executed on the framing alone and now returns `Nothing to execute`. Builds on the directory from #6947. ## The finding that reshaped this PR I set out to make `resources.subscribe` revision-conditional — advertise it to `2025-11-25` clients, withhold it from `2026-07-28` ones. [{"number":6964,"title":"fix(github-copilot): verify model invocability at sync, surface an actionable model-not-supported error","body":"Fixes T-959: chat on the GitHub Copilot provider could fail with `400 {"message": "The requested model is not supported.", "type": "api_validation_error"}` for models Archestra itself offered in the model picker. ## Root cause Copilot's `/models` is not an invocability catalog. Verified against a live subscription: 13 of the 24 entries our static filter kept were rejected outright by `/chat/completions` with `model_not_supported` — retired aliases listed next to their still-working snapshots (`gpt-4` vs `gpt-4o`, `gpt-3.5-turbo` vs `gpt-3.5-turbo-0613`), client-internal agent models (`copilot-search-*`, `exec-agent-*`), and per-plan-unavailable models that still declare `"/chat/completions"` in `supported_endpoints`. No catalog field discriminates dead from alive entries (a dead alias can be field-identical to a working model, down to `version`), and on the verified plan every entry is `model_picker_enabled: false`, so no static filter can compute the usable set. GitHub's own clients avoid the problem only because their picker never exposes these entries. ## Fix **Verify invocability during model sync.** CAPI validates the model before the payload, so a deliberately invalid `{"model": …, "messages": []}` request is a zero-inference oracle: a dead model answers `model_not_supported`, a live one answers "messages must be non-empty". Nothing is generated and no model is ever invoked, so the probe cannot consume premium requests. The fetcher now probes every statically-kept candidate (8 concurrent) and drops only definite `model_not_supported` answers — 429/5xx/network failures keep the model, so an upstream outage degrades to the previous unverified catalog rather than an empty one. Runs everywhere the fetcher is used: connect-time key validation, lazy re-sync, explicit sync, and the proxy `/models` listing. **Actionable error for the residual window.** A conversation can stay pinned to a model that has since died (the proxy's error wrapping keeps `message`/`type` but drops the upstream `code`). The chat error mapper now classifies Copilot's model-not-supported 400 as `NotFound` — "The selected model is not available. Please choose a different model." — instead of the retry-suggesting invalid-request copy, which misleads on a deterministic rejection. ## Testing - New proxy route tests drive the real adapter and Copilot fetch wrapper (token exchange + editor-identity headers) against a faked wire, pinning that the catalogued model name goes upstream and the upstream 400 surfaces for both streaming and non-streaming. - New chat stream test pins that a github-copilot conversation's model FK is dereferenced to the provider model name before dispatch. - Fetcher tests cover the verification: a listed-but-rejected model is dropped, probes only target statically-kept candidates, inconclusive probes (429/network) keep the model. - Error-mapper tests cover the NotFound classification and that other Copilot 400s keep the generic invalid-request code. - Live validation on a dev stack with a real subscription: synced catalog went from 24 models (13 dead) to the invocable set; picking any listed model chats successfully; a conversation pinned to a dead model shows the actionable copy. --- ","state":"closed","draft":false,"merged":false,"html_url":"https://github.com/archestra-ai/archestra/pull/6964","user":{"login":"piercypixel","id":13911621,"profile_url":"https://github.com/piercypixel","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/13911621?v=4"},"requested_reviewers":["iskhakov"],"head":{"ref":"piercypixel/t959-copilot-model-not-supported","sha":"d1bb0ce678ac7421e681223bcf937c8313a52c8f","repo":{"full_name":"archestra-ai/archestra","description":"Enterprise AI Platform with guardrails, MCP registry, gateway & orchestrator"}},"base":{"ref":"main","sha":"1a1fd231e171822cd869f84c7e3346b59e76fbfb","repo":{"full_name":"archestra-ai/archestra","description":"Enterprise AI Platform with guardrails, MCP registry, gateway & orchestrator"}},"created_at":"2026-07-29T16:39:49Z","updated_at":"2026-07-29T17:00:12Z","closed_at":"2026-07-29T17:00:10Z","merged_at":"2026-07-29T17:00:10Z"},{"number":6963,"title":"fix(apps): bound app tool calls at the LLM ceiling and cancel abandoned calls","body":"## Summary An app's `archestra.llm.complete()` rejected with `MCP error -32001: Request timed out` whenever the attached model needed more than 60 seconds — which reasoning models routinely do, since the app path is the platform's only non-streaming LLM call and all thinking time accumulates into the single response (T-981). The timer was the MCP SDK's default request timeout in the app iframe's guest client: the SDK passed no request options to `callServerTool`, and nothing downstream was stricter, so the guest always lost the race while the backend kept generating (and the proxy kept billing) a result nobody would receive. Live measurement on a dev stack: the app showed the error at exactly 60s while the same completion returned HTTP 200 at 100s and was recorded in LLM logs ~40s after the app had already failed. The guest now bounds host tool calls at 10 minutes, matching the platform's own upstream LLM client ceiling (`ANTHROPIC_CLIENT_TIMEOUT_MS`) rather than gating stricter than it. Cancellation travels the whole chain: the guest's timeout or teardown aborts the host bridge's fetch via the `oncalltool` handler's `extra.signal`; the app proxy route closes the per-request transport when the client disconnects, which makes the protocol abort the in-flight handler's signal; that signal reaches `executeArchestraTool` (as the existing `context.abortSignal`) and `executeToolCallForOwner` (its existing `abortSignal` option); and an aborted LLM completion stops quietly instead of logging an error and claiming `llm_unavailable`. Two route-level details deserve reviewer attention. In JSON-response mode an aborted handler never produces a response, so `transport.handleRequest` never settles — the route races it against the client-disconnect path instead of awaiting it bare. And an aborted request leaves its transport closed mid-flight, so the per-(app,user) cached server is evicted rather than released for reuse; the cache's exclusive `acquire` guarantees the closed transport can only ever belong to the aborted request. ## Validation - `app-sdk-runtime.test.ts`: the guest-module stub now honors the MCP SDK's request-options timeout contract; new tests pin that a 3-minute completion resolves (red before this fix, failing with the exact reported error) and that a completion beyond the 10-minute ceiling still times out. - `app-llm.test.ts`: an aborted call cancels the model call and reports cancellation, not a provider failure. - Live on a dev stack with a reasoning model (glm-5.1): a 188-second completion resolves in the real iframe chain where it previously died at 60s; killing the viewer 25 seconds into a call produced the cancelled tool-call record within ~1 second. ## Follow-up The LLM proxy's non-streaming handlers do not tie their own upstream request to their client's disconnect, so a cancelled completion can still run to completion inside the proxy and record the interaction (observed landing two minutes after the abort). That gap predates this change, spans every provider adapter, and equally affects non-streamed chat cancellation — left for its own change. No docs change: the apps page never promised a timeout, and the fix restores its documented behavior (`llm.complete` resolves to the model's text). --- ","state":"closed","draft":false,"merged":false,"html_url":"https://github.com/archestra-ai/archestra/pull/6963","user":{"login":"piercypixel","id":13911621,"profile_url":"https://github.com/piercypixel","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/13911621?v=4"},"requested_reviewers":["iskhakov"],"head":{"ref":"piercypixel/t981-app-reasoning-timeout","sha":"16d15550f6fcc7dfed3fd8a0147db610cc340941","repo":{"full_name":"archestra-ai/archestra","description":"Enterprise AI Platform with guardrails, MCP registry, gateway & orchestrator"}},"base":{"ref":"main","sha":"1a1fd231e171822cd869f84c7e3346b59e76fbfb","repo":{"full_name":"archestra-ai/archestra","description":"Enterprise AI Platform with guardrails, MCP registry, gateway & orchestrator"}},"created_at":"2026-07-29T16:38:35Z","updated_at":"2026-07-29T17:06:40Z","closed_at":"2026-07-29T17:06:38Z","merged_at":"2026-07-29T17:06:38Z"},{"number":6962,"title":"fix(llm-pricing): read Amazon's global-endpoint price marker for Nova","body":"## Summary The vendored AWS snapshot identifies a global-endpoint SKU by a `_Global` suffix on the usage type. That is Anthropic's and TwelveLabs' convention. Amazon's own Nova models mark it `-cross-region-global` instead, so no global entry was ever transcribed for them — and worse, the single entry that was transcribed crossed the two tiers: `Nova 2.0 Lite` held a regional input beside a global output, a pair AWS charges at neither endpoint. `Nova 2.0 Omni` was wrong the same way. `Nova 2.0 Pro` had a correct regional entry but no global one, so a `global.` profile silently paid the regional rate. Re-read from the offer document, standard on-demand, text dimensions only: | model | regional | global | |---|---|---| | Nova 2.0 Lite | 0.33 / 2.75 | 0.30 / 2.50 | | Nova 2.0 Omni | 0.30 / 2.80 | 0.30 / 2.50 | | Nova 2.0 Pro | 1.375 / 11 | 1.25 / 10 | Omni's input is genuinely the same on both tiers; only its output carries the premium. It does not follow the uniform 1.1× uplift the Claude listings show, which is why the values are read per dimension rather than derived from one. A sweep of both offer documents confirms the split is exactly these three models: everything else publishing a global SKU uses `_Global`. `Nova Sonic 2.0` is deliberately untouched. It splits its dimensions by modality, and the stored 0.33/2.75 is its text pair; the 3.00 sitting beside it is `speech-input-tokens` and belongs to a different meter. Both conventions are now recorded in the transcription rules, since reading either one wrongly produces a price that looks plausible. ## Verification A test asserts the regional and global tiers resolve to different prices for `amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0`; it fails against the previous snapshot, where both ids collapsed onto the one mixed entry. A standing guard asserts no `|global` entry is priced above its regional counterpart — crossing the tiers is what produced an entry neither endpoint bills at. It covers all ten global entries. `Nova 2.0 Omni` and `Nova 2.0 Pro` have no `AWS_PRICE_IDENTITY` mapping yet, so their entries are latent until a deployment serves those ids; `Nova 2.0 Lite` is mapped and live. --- ","state":"open","draft":false,"merged":false,"html_url":"https://github.com/archestra-ai/archestra/pull/6962","user":{"login":"divineforest","id":22360,"profile_url":"https://github.com/divineforest","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/22360?v=4"},"head":{"ref":"fix/bedrock-nova-global-endpoint-prices","sha":"9b39445016b511141ba55bf847076ba37492124a","repo":{"full_name":"archestra-ai/archestra","description":"Enterprise AI Platform with guardrails, MCP registry, gateway & orchestrator"}},"base":{"ref":"main","sha":"2cb4a589217f3511054924e1e5e8e5de7b290b72","repo":{"full_name":"archestra-ai/archestra","description":"Enterprise AI Platform with guardrails, MCP registry, gateway & orchestrator"}},"created_at":"2026-07-29T15:09:53Z","updated_at":"2026-07-29T15:10:05Z"},{"number":6961,"title":"fix(llm-cost): stop rounding model prices to the cent before costing them","body":"## Summary `getEffectivePricing` formatted the per-million price with `toFixed(2)`, and every cost path parses that string back: `interactions.cost` via `kb-interaction.ts`, token-cost limits in `limit.ts`, and optimization-rule savings in `cost-optimization.ts`. The rounding is therefore a billing error rather than a display choice. A model published at $0.035/M was costed at $0.04 — 14% high across 45 rows today — and anything under $0.005/M would have recorded as free. Storage was never the problem. The columns are `numeric(20,12)` and hold `0.000000035` exactly; the precision died at the read boundary. Cache prices already had this fix, with a comment stating that 2-decimal rounding "would be materially lossy here". Input and output simply never got the same treatment, which is why the models table has been rendering `$1.00` beside an unpadded `$0.1` cache price all along. The helper is now shared rather than cache-specific. Padding moves to the reading end, so `$50.00` still renders as `$50.00` while `$0.035` survives intact, and all four price columns agree. That works but produces awkward `for_each` / `lookup` boilerplate at every callsite, and the list endpoints paginate exhaustively.

Proposed: four singular data sources that hit the backend's by-id (or by-name) GET endpoints directly, surface a clean 404 diagnostic, and expose the row's full attribute set. Matches the AWS/GCP convention of pairing `aws_iam_role` (singular) with `aws_iam_roles` (plural).","state":"OPEN","user":{"login":"priyanshu0x"},"created_at":"2026-05-21T15:50:36Z","updated_at":"2026-05-21T15:50:36Z"},{"number":123,"title":"feat(agent): surface built_in Computed flag","body":"The provider's `archestra_agent` exposes `built_in_agent_config` for managing platform built-in agents (the dual-LLM / policy-configuration subagents auto-seeded by the backend), but there's no way to read back whether a given agent is actually a platform built-in. Operators importing an existing agent can't write conditional HCL on it.

Proposed: expose `built_in` as a Computed bool, refreshed from the backend's `builtIn` field. Documents the `built_in_agent_config` block's "only meaningful when `built_in = true`; backend silently ignores it on user-created agents" semantic so the expected workflow (import + manage existing) is discoverable from the schema docs.","state":"OPEN","user":{"login":"priyanshu0x"},"created_at":"2026-05-21T15:49:16Z","updated_at":"2026-05-21T15:49:16Z"},{"number":121,"title":"feat(incoming_email): expose org-singleton incoming-email webhook subscription","body":"The platform exposes inbound email-to-agent routing via Microsoft Graph (and a pluggable provider abstraction), but configuring the org-level subscription requires hand-rolled curl against `POST /api/incoming-email/setup`. Operators running multi-environment installs can't keep webhook URLs in version control.

Proposed: `archestra_incoming_email` — an org-singleton resource holding `webhook_url` (Required, HTTPS-validated) and surfacing the platform's `subscription_id` / `provider` / `expires_at` / `is_active` as Computed. Update = re-setup (backend tears down the prior subscription before creating a new one), Delete maps to `DELETE /api/incoming-email/subscription`. Proposed: two one-shot resources (`archestra_mcp_server_reauthenticate`, `archestra_mcp_server_reinstall`) modeled like `archestra_tool_policy_auto_config` — all inputs `RequiresReplace`, an opaque `trigger` string the user bumps to re-issue the call, no-op Read/Delete because the underlying install row is owned by `archestra_mcp_server_installation`.","state":"OPEN","user":{"login":"priyanshu0x"},"created_at":"2026-05-21T15:44:45Z","updated_at":"2026-05-21T15:44:45Z"},{"number":117,"title":"Add archestra_agent_delegation resource","body":"## Summary

Agents (and MCP gateways) can sub-delegate work to other internal agents via `POST /api/agents/{id}/delegations`. The provider doesn't surface this, so operators wire delegations through the UI today.

## Proposal

Add `archestra_agent_delegation` — owns the per-agent set of delegation targets. Authoritative over the agent's full delegation list; the backend's sync endpoint replaces all existing delegations with the new set, so adding/removing `target_agent_ids` patches in place (no `RequiresReplace`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Resource registered as `archestra_agent_delegation`.
- [ ] Schema: `agent_id` (Required, RequiresReplace — 1:1 keyed on source agent), `target_agent_ids` (Required Set, size ≥ 1); Computed `id` (== `agent_id`).
- [ ] Create/Update both call the sync endpoint; Delete calls sync with empty array (backend rejects null).
- [ ] LLM proxies reject delegation with backend 400 — provider relays the error verbatim (plan-time check would need an extra round-trip to discover `agent_type`).
- [ ] ImportState by bare source `agent_id`.
- [ ] Acceptance tests cover full Create → Update (add/remove targets, no replacement) → idempotent re-apply → Import lifecycle, plus the LLM-proxy 400 rejection.","state":"OPEN","user":{"login":"priyanshu0x"},"created_at":"2026-05-21T10:55:01Z","updated_at":"2026-05-21T10:55:01Z"}],"totalCount":17,"pageInfo":{"hasNextPage":true,"hasPreviousPage":false,"startCursor":"Y3Vyc29yOnYyOpK0MjAyNi0wNS0yMVQxNTo1MDozNlrPAAAAAQv7UiM=","endCursor":"Y3Vyc29yOnYyOpK0MjAyNi0wNS0yMVQxMDo1NTowMVrPAAAAAQvb_HU="}}

      document.getElementById("copy-card-btn").addEventListener("click", () => {
        if (!globalReportData) return;
        const text = `The Commit Whisperer Roast for @${globalReportData.username}:\nPersonality: ${globalReportData.personality}\nRoast: ${globalReportData.roast}\nChaos Score: ${globalReportData.chaosScore}%\n#TheCommitWhisperer`;
        try {
          navigator.clipboard.writeText(text);
          const btn = document.getElementById("copy-card-btn");
          btn.textContent = "Copied to Clipboard! 🎉";
          setTimeout(() => btn.textContent = "Copy Roast Summary 📋", 2000);
        } catch(e) {
          alert(text);
        }
      });
    });

    const loadingSteps = [
      "Extracting secret commit messages in parallel...",
      "Scanning branches and pull requests...",
      "Consulting the Ancient Git Oracle for unique roast..."
    ];

    function renderReport(data) {
      document.getElementById("res-avatar").src = data.avatarUrl;
      document.getElementById("res-name").textContent = data.name;
      document.getElementById("res-username").textContent = "@" + data.username;
      document.getElementById("res-bio").textContent = data.bio;
      document.getElementById("res-chaos-score").textContent = data.chaosScore + "%";
      document.getElementById("res-personality").textContent = data.personality;
      document.getElementById("res-roast").textContent = data.roast;
      document.getElementById("res-secret").textContent = `"${data.secretCommitMeaning}"`;
      document.getElementById("res-oracle").textContent = data.oracleVerdict;

      document.getElementById("stat-repos").textContent = data.reposCount;
      document.getElementById("stat-commits").textContent = data.totalCommitsCount;
      document.getElementById("stat-prs").textContent = data.pullRequests ? data.pullRequests.length : 0;

      // Render Awards
      const awardsContainer = document.getElementById("res-awards");
      awardsContainer.innerHTML = "";
      if (data.awards && Array.isArray(data.awards)) {
        data.awards.forEach(award => {
          awardsContainer.innerHTML += `
            <div class="award-item">
              <div class="award-icon">${award.icon}</div>
              <div class="award-content">
                <h4>${award.title}</h4>
                <p>${award.desc}</p>
              </div>
            </div>
          `;
        });
      }

      // Render Confessions
      const confessionsContainer = document.getElementById("res-confessions");
      confessionsContainer.innerHTML = "";
      if (data.commitMessages && data.commitMessages.length > 0) {
        data.commitMessages.slice(0, 5).forEach(c => {
          confessionsContainer.innerHTML += `
            <div class="confession-box">
              <strong>[${c.repo}]</strong> "${c.message}"
            </div>
          `;
        });
      } else {
        confessionsContainer.innerHTML = `<div class="confession-box">No recent commit messages found. Pure ghost mode!</div>`;
      }

      document.querySelector(".search-card").style.display = "block";
      document.getElementById("report-container").style.display = "block";
    }

    async function triggerAnalysis() {
      let inputVal = document.getElementById("target-input").value.trim();
      const errToast = document.getElementById("error-toast");
      errToast.style.display = "none";
      errToast.textContent = "";

      if (!inputVal) {
        errToast.textContent = "Please enter a GitHub username or repository (e.g. owner/repo).";
        errToast.style.display = "block";
        return;
      }

      document.querySelector(".search-card").style.display = "none";
      const loadingStage = document.getElementById("loading-stage");
      loadingStage.style.display = "block";

      let stepIdx = 0;
      const stepInterval = setInterval(() => {
        stepIdx = (stepIdx + 1) % loadingSteps.length;
        document.getElementById("loading-step-text").textContent = loadingSteps[stepIdx];
      }, 600);

      try {
        let repos = [];
        let userProfile = null;

        // Check if input is owner/repo or username
        if (inputVal.includes('/')) {
          const parts = inputVal.split('/');
          const owner = parts[0];
          const repo = parts[1];
          repos = [{ name: repo, owner: { login: owner } }];
          userProfile = { login: owner, name: owner, avatar_url: `https://github.com/${owner}.png`, bio: "GitHub Repository Owner." };
        } else {
          // Fetch user profile info first
          try {
            const me = await archestra.tools.call("github__get_me", {});
            if (me && me.login.toLowerCase() === inputVal.toLowerCase()) {
              userProfile = {
                login: me.login,
                name: me.details?.name || me.name || me.login,
                bio: me.details?.bio || me.bio || "Developer on GitHub.",
                avatar_url: me.avatar_url || `https://github.com/${me.login}.png`
              };
            }
          } catch(e) {}

          if (!userProfile) {
            userProfile = {
              login: inputVal,
              name: inputVal,
              bio: "GitHub User.",
              avatar_url: `https://github.com/${inputVal}.png`
            };
          }

          // Search repositories for user
          try {
            const repoRes = await archestra.tools.call("github__search_repositories", { query: `user:${inputVal}` });
            if (repoRes && repoRes.items) {
              repos = repoRes.items.slice(0, 3);
            }
          } catch (e) {
            console.warn("Repo search error", e);
          }
        }

        if (repos.length === 0) {
          clearInterval(stepInterval);
          loadingStage.style.display = "none";
          document.querySelector(".search-card").style.display = "block";
          errToast.textContent = `No public repositories found for "${inputVal}". Please try another username or specific repository (owner/repo).`;
          errToast.style.display = "block";
          return;
        }

        // Fetch data for repos in parallel using Promise.all
        let commitMessages = [];
        let branchesList = [];
        let prsList = [];
        let issuesList = [];
        let totalCommitsCount = 0;

        const repoPromises = repos.map(async (repo) => {
          const ownerLogin = repo.owner?.login || inputVal;
          const repoName = repo.name;

          const [commitRes, branchRes, prRes, issueRes] = await Promise.all([
            archestra.tools.call("github__list_commits", { owner: ownerLogin, repo: repoName, perPage: 10 }).catch(() => []),
            archestra.tools.call("github__list_branches", { owner: ownerLogin, repo: repoName, perPage: 5 }).catch(() => []),
            archestra.tools.call("github__list_pull_requests", { owner: ownerLogin, repo: repoName, state: "all", perPage: 5 }).catch(() => []),
            archestra.tools.call("github__list_issues", { owner: ownerLogin, repo: repoName, state: "ALL", perPage: 5 }).catch(() => [])
          ]);

          if (Array.isArray(commitRes)) {
            totalCommitsCount += commitRes.length;
            commitRes.forEach(c => {
              if (c.commit && c.commit.message) {
                commitMessages.push({ repo: repoName, message: c.commit.message.split('\n')[0] });
              }
            });
          }

          if (Array.isArray(branchRes)) {
            branchRes.forEach(b => branchesList.push({ repo: repoName, name: b.name }));
          }

          if (Array.isArray(prRes)) {
            prRes.forEach(p => prsList.push({ repo: repoName, title: p.title, state: p.state }));
          }

          if (Array.isArray(issueRes)) {
            issueRes.forEach(i => issuesList.push({ repo: repoName, title: i.title, state: i.state }));
          }
        });

        await Promise.all(repoPromises);

        clearInterval(stepInterval);
        loadingStage.style.display = "none";

        const dataSummary = {
          username: userProfile.login,
          name: userProfile.name,
          bio: userProfile.bio,
          avatarUrl: userProfile.avatar_url,
          reposCount: repos.length,
          totalCommitsCount: totalCommitsCount,
          commitMessages: commitMessages,
          branches: branchesList,
          pullRequests: prsList,
          issues: issuesList
        };

        if (dataSummary.totalCommitsCount === 0 && dataSummary.commitMessages.length === 0 && dataSummary.branches.length === 0) {
          document.querySelector(".search-card").style.display = "block";
          errToast.textContent = `Target "${inputVal}" has insufficient public commit or repository activity to generate a unique roast. Try another active user or repository!`;
          errToast.style.display = "block";
          return;
        }

        const uniqueSeed = Date.now() + Math.random();
        const llmPrompt = `You are an elite, brutally funny senior tech lead and roast master. Analyze this specific developer's exact GitHub activity data below and generate a completely unique, highly customized roast and personality profile. DO NOT use generic templates or canned responses; specifically reference their actual commit messages, branch names, PR titles, and repo stats provided below.
Seed: ${uniqueSeed}

Real Developer Activity Data:
Username: ${dataSummary.username}
Name: ${dataSummary.name}
Bio: ${dataSummary.bio}
Repositories Scanned: ${dataSummary.reposCount}
Total Commits Scanned: ${dataSummary.totalCommitsCount}
Commit Messages: ${JSON.stringify(dataSummary.commitMessages)}
Branches: ${JSON.stringify(dataSummary.branches)}
Pull Requests: ${JSON.stringify(dataSummary.pullRequests)}
Issues: ${JSON.stringify(dataSummary.issues)}

Return a JSON object (strictly valid JSON only, no markdown wrapping, no backticks) with exact keys:
{
  "personality": "A custom funny developer persona title tailored specifically to their commit messages and branch names",
  "roast": "A 3-sentence devastatingly witty roast citing specific words or themes from their actual commit messages or PR titles.",
  "secretCommitMeaning": "What their specific commit messages secretly reveal about their psychological state",
  "chaosScore": integer between 25 and 99,
  "awards": [
    {"title": "Custom Award Title 1", "desc": "Funny description citing specific data points", "icon": "🏆"},
    {"title": "Custom Award Title 2", "desc": "Funny description citing specific repo activity", "icon": "⚡"},
    {"title": "Custom Award Title 3", "desc": "Funny description citing specific commit habits", "icon": "💀"}
  ],
  "oracleVerdict": "A dramatic 2-sentence prophetic summary of their engineering destiny based precisely on their provided codebase activity."
}`;

        let report;
        try {
          const llmRes = await archestra.llm.complete(llmPrompt, { jsonMode: true });
          let cleanJson = llmRes.trim();
          if (cleanJson.startsWith("```")) {
            cleanJson = cleanJson.replace(/^```(json)?/, "").replace(/```$/, "").trim();
          }
          report = JSON.parse(cleanJson);
        } catch (e) {
          console.warn("LLM parse fallback", e);
          const sampleMsg = commitMessages[0]?.message || "wip";
          const sampleBranch = branchesList[0]?.name || "feature-1";
          report = {
            personality: `The '${sampleBranch.toUpperCase()}' Branch Hoarder`,
            roast: `Analyzing @${dataSummary.username} reveals someone whose commit message "${sampleMsg}" truly captures the essence of living on the edge. With ${dataSummary.totalCommitsCount} commits across ${dataSummary.reposCount} repos, every push is a masterclass in controlled panic.`,
            secretCommitMeaning: `Your commits prove you type before you think and debug with git log --all --graph.`,
            chaosScore: Math.floor(Math.random() * 40) + 60,
            awards: [
              { title: "Branch Hoarding Champion", desc: `Famous for keeping branches like '${sampleBranch}' alive indefinitely.`, icon: "🌿" },
              { title: "Cryptic Commit Poet", desc: `Author of legendary messages such as: "${sampleMsg}".`, icon: "📜" },
              { title: "CI/CD Stress-Tester", desc: "Pushing directly to main to see if GitHub Actions breaks.", icon: "💣" }
            ],
            oracleVerdict: `Your codebase is a archaeological dig of hasty fixes and triumphant merges. May your tests pass on the first try.`
          };
        }

        globalReportData = {
          ...dataSummary,
          ...report
        };

        // Save to user storage for persistence across reloads/chats
        try {
          await archestra.storage.user.set("latest_roast_report", globalReportData);
        } catch (e) {
          console.warn("Failed to persist report to storage", e);
        }

        renderReport(globalReportData);

      } catch (err) {
        clearInterval(stepInterval);
        loadingStage.style.display = "none";
        document.querySelector(".search-card").style.display = "block";
        errToast.textContent = "Error analyzing user: " + (err.message || err);
        errToast.style.display = "block";
      }
    }
  </script>


</body><grammarly-desktop-integration data-grammarly-shadow-root="true" style="visibility: visible !important;"></grammarly-desktop-integration></html>
